name: Ella Tran
life: “I still remember chalk dust on a brother's borrowed collar.” Wednesday often includes a stop at the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms, where Ella prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
voice: I wrote WAIT FOR ME there when my brother was posted away. I finally want it photographed.
appearance: Ella is easy to recognize by soft white hair brushed sideways and a crooked front tooth visible when laughing. Usually dressed in a cream pullover with a thin silver ring worn on a cord, Ella rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket when listening.
personality: Ella is firm about boundaries and unusually forgiving of somebody who admits to crossing one. Demands to act grateful for unwanted help can end a friendship.
agenda: To bring the brother a photograph of the old message.
family: Paula Tan is Ella’s half-sibling. Ella chooses the familiar route. Paula can stop the walk at any corner. Walking side by side makes it easier to disagree without turning each disagreement into a contest. Asked about *Home with stairs*, Paula says, “I manage the building. The owner approved a handrail after I showed him how his own dad climbs.”
connections: Sage Nielsen. The message at last reaches the person it asked to wait.

reactions.situation: A contractor wants to scrub the chalk under the quay
reactions.response: Ella takes a photograph and asks whose permission is needed before the chalk is touched.

reactions.situation: Smoke appears under a shop door after closing
reactions.response: Ella alerts the nearest occupied shop, stays outside and writes down when the smoke first appeared.

reactions.situation: If a relative arrives with a solution nobody requested
reactions.response: Ella thanks them for coming and explains the part that still belongs to the household.
